research_methodology.consolidation_threshold: Fewer than 3 substantive verifiable facts OR no Midwest CNC brand-tie relevance
research_methodology.distance_method: Haversine great-circle distance from Waterloo, IA (42.49°N, 92.34°W) × 1.20 road-factor multiplier

des-moines-iowa.name: Des Moines
des-moines-iowa.manufacturing_summary: Historically a coal mining center; current economy dominated by insurance/financial HQs. Corteva (ag biotech) and Amazon distribution provide ag-adjacent and logistics manufacturing presence. No direct heavy-CNC manufacturer base in Des Moines proper, but the city sits at the center of Iowa's ag-equipment supply chain.
des-moines-iowa.decision_rationale: Iowa state capital, 109 miles from Waterloo, sits inside the ag-equipment supply chain. Service framing leans on Corteva (ag biotech) and proximity to John Deere Waterloo + Quad Cities clusters.

davenport-iowa.name: Davenport
major_employers: John Deere (948 at north Davenport plant)
davenport-iowa.manufacturing_summary: John Deere is the second-largest Quad Cities employer with the north Davenport plant. Historical manufacturing included locomotives, meat-packing, Caterpillar loaders, and wheel manufacture. Part of the Quad Cities heavy-machinery cluster.

waterloo-iowa.name: Waterloo
waterloo-iowa.manufacturing_summary: John Deere has manufactured tractors, engines, and agricultural machinery in Waterloo for over a century. Tyson Foods meatpacking is a major operation. Home base for Midwest CNC Services.

cedar-rapids-iowa.name: Cedar Rapids
cedar-rapids-iowa.manufacturing_summary: One of the largest corn-processing cities in the world; grain processing alone employs roughly 4,000. Quaker Oats has operated since 1873. Collins Aerospace anchors aerospace manufacturing.

iowa-city-iowa.name: Iowa City
iowa-city-iowa.manufacturing_summary: Wikipedia article does not describe a current manufacturing sector. Economy dominated by healthcare, education, and service sectors.
iowa-city-iowa.decision_rationale: No verifiable manufacturing employers or industrial parks. Healthcare/education-only economy doesn't justify a standalone CNC service page.

ames-iowa.name: Ames
ames-iowa.manufacturing_summary: Hosts Ames National Laboratory (DOE materials research) and largest federal animal disease center. Manufacturing presence includes Danfoss and Hach Chemical. ISU Research Park is a business incubator.
ames-iowa.decision_rationale: Danfoss + Hach + ISU Research Park provide a verifiable manufacturing/R&D base. Framing leans on the research-park + ag-research context.

chicago-illinois.name: Chicago
chicago-illinois.manufacturing_summary: Chicago produced more steel than the United Kingdom during WWII; steel employment dropped from 250,000 (1960s) to 28,000 (2015). Modern economy emphasizes finance, but the metro retains a deep industrial supply chain.
chicago-illinois.decision_rationale: Largest city in our service area by population (2.7M). Even with industrial decline noted, the Chicago metro retains a substantial machine-shop base feeding aerospace, defense, and heavy industry.

naperville-illinois.name: Naperville
naperville-illinois.manufacturing_summary: Inside the Illinois Technology and Research Corridor. Hosts Kraft Foods' plant supplying all North American Triscuit production and Dukane Precast's double-wall precast concrete plant.

peoria-illinois.name: Peoria
peoria-illinois.manufacturing_summary: Caterpillar Inc. was Peoria-headquartered for over 110 years (HQ moved to Deerfield 2017, Irving TX 2022) but Caterpillar operations remain. Komatsu America operates a major heavy-equipment manufacturing facility.
peoria-illinois.decision_rationale: Caterpillar + Komatsu give Peoria one of the strongest heavy-equipment manufacturing concentrations in Illinois.

rockford-illinois.name: Rockford
rockford-illinois.manufacturing_summary: Rockford transitioned from agricultural machinery to fastener manufacturing and aerospace. Collins Aerospace (rooted in Sundstrand Corporation) and Woodward Inc. (opened a $200M campus in Loves Park in 2012) anchor the precision machining base.
rockford-illinois.decision_rationale: Historic 'machine tool city' with Collins Aerospace, Woodward, Stellantis. One of the highest-value city pages in the network.

springfield-illinois.name: Springfield
springfield-illinois.manufacturing_summary: Wikipedia article does not describe a current manufacturing sector. Government-dominated economy.
springfield-illinois.decision_rationale: State capital with government-dominated economy and no manufacturing employers verifiable from Wikipedia. 301 to Illinois state page.

milwaukee-wisconsin.name: Milwaukee
milwaukee-wisconsin.manufacturing_summary: Milwaukee is a recognized manufacturing center anchored by Harley-Davidson and Rockwell Automation, alongside a heritage of brewing (Miller, Pabst, Schlitz).

madison-wisconsin.name: Madison
madison-wisconsin.manufacturing_summary: Madison hosts a large biotech/health-IT scene (Epic, Exact Sciences, Promega) plus Trek Bicycle, Sub-Zero & Wolf appliances, and Spectrum Brands manufacturing operations.

green-bay-wisconsin.name: Green Bay
green-bay-wisconsin.manufacturing_summary: Known as the 'Toilet Paper Capital of the World' for its concentration of paper companies (Georgia-Pacific, Procter & Gamble). Meatpacking via JBS and American Foods Group.

kenosha-wisconsin.name: Kenosha
kenosha-wisconsin.manufacturing_summary: From 1902–1988 produced millions of automobiles (Nash, Hudson, AMC). Has since transitioned to light industrial and distribution. Snap-on Tools is HQ'd here.

racine-wisconsin.name: Racine
racine-wisconsin.manufacturing_summary: Racine was a 'factory town almost from the beginning' — early center of car/motorcycle manufacturing. Now anchored by Case IH (ag equipment), Modine (heat exchangers), and S.C. Johnson.

minneapolis-minnesota.name: Minneapolis
minneapolis-minnesota.manufacturing_summary: Medtronic was founded in a Minneapolis garage in 1949 and remains anchored to the metro. Thermo King invented mobile refrigeration here. Minneapolis-Honeywell developed precision instrumentation for military contracts.

st-paul-minnesota.name: St. Paul
st-paul-minnesota.manufacturing_summary: 3M moved to Saint Paul in 1910; Ford's Twin Cities Assembly Plant operated in Highland Park (1924–2011). Modern economy retains chemical, financial, and industrial-supply manufacturing.

rochester-minnesota.name: Rochester
rochester-minnesota.manufacturing_summary: Rochester Technology Campus formerly housed IBM midrange and Blue Gene prototype production. McNeilus Truck manufactures heavy trucks. Kerry Group produces fermented ingredients for food processing.

duluth-minnesota.name: Duluth
industrial_parks: Morgan Park (former U.S. Steel company town)
duluth-minnesota.manufacturing_summary: U.S. Steel's Duluth Works opened 1915; modern manufacturing emphasizes Cirrus Aircraft (general aviation manufacturer). Port handles iron ore, coal, grain, limestone, cement, and wind-turbine parts.

bloomington-minnesota.name: Bloomington
bloomington-minnesota.manufacturing_summary: Toro relocated to Bloomington in 1952. Manufacturing employers include Donaldson Company (filtration) and Seagate Technology. Bloomington supports 100,000+ regional jobs.

omaha-nebraska.name: Omaha
omaha-nebraska.manufacturing_summary: The Glenn L. Martin Company produced 521 B-29 Superfortresses here in WWII. Union Stockyards (est. 1883) anchored meatpacking. Modern industrial base centers on railroads, construction, and food processing.

lincoln-nebraska.name: Lincoln
lincoln-nebraska.manufacturing_summary: Kawasaki Motors Manufacturing is one of Lincoln's largest private employers (2,400+) producing ATVs, utility vehicles, personal watercraft, and passenger rail cars.

bellevue-nebraska.name: Bellevue
bellevue-nebraska.manufacturing_summary: Wikipedia article does not describe current civilian industrial manufacturing. Offutt AFB is the dominant employer.
bellevue-nebraska.decision_rationale: Single military-base employer; no verifiable civilian manufacturing or industrial cluster. 301 to Nebraska state page.

grand-island-nebraska.name: Grand Island
grand-island-nebraska.manufacturing_summary: Home to the first U.S. sugar beet processing factory (c. 1890). Hornady manufactures ammunition. Major freight rail hub.

kearney-nebraska.name: Kearney
kearney-nebraska.manufacturing_summary: Baldwin Filters is the top manufacturing employer (1,000+). West Pharmaceutical Services and Eaton Corporation maintain regional operations.

north-platte-nebraska.name: North Platte
major_employers: Union Pacific Railroad (1,700+ at Bailey Yard)
north-platte-nebraska.manufacturing_summary: Home to Bailey Yard, the world's largest rail yard. Sustainable Beef meatpacking opened May 2025. Limited heavy-industrial machining base beyond rail.
north-platte-nebraska.decision_rationale: Rail-hub anchor is real and verifiable, but CNC-machining tie-back is weak (rail yards run service shops, not precision machining). 644 miles from Waterloo. Aaron review: ENRICH with rail-shop framing, or CONSOLIDATE.

framing_constraints.industry_tie: western Nebraska freight-in spindle rebuilds + ag-implement and rail-adjacent shop work
framing_constraints.rationale: Aaron-approved with constraint: rail tie-back is honest but weak; ag-implement framing for the brand pages

st-louis-missouri.name: St. Louis
major_employers: Boeing Defense, Space & Security (largest STL employer)
Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
st-louis-missouri.manufacturing_summary: Boeing Defense, Space & Security is the largest St. Louis employer (referenced in Aaron's state-brief, verified by independent reporting); aerospace concentration is the defining industrial cluster. Anheuser-Busch maintains brewing operations.
st-louis-missouri.decision_rationale: Boeing Defense is the anchor employer. Wikipedia's St. Louis article didn't expand on Boeing detail in the fetch but the fact is well-established via multiple independent sources and Aaron's state-brief.

kansas-city-missouri.name: Kansas City
industrial_parks: Bannister Federal Complex (houses Honeywell Kansas City Plant)
kansas-city-missouri.manufacturing_summary: The Honeywell Kansas City Plant (NNSA facility) produces 85% of the non-nuclear components of the U.S. nuclear bomb arsenal. Sanofi-Aventis operates a major pharmaceutical plant.

springfield-missouri.name: Springfield
springfield-missouri.manufacturing_summary: Regional center for distribution, logistics, and manufacturing. Manufacturing employers include Paul Mueller Co., Positronic, Prime Inc., and Springfield ReManufacturing.

columbia-missouri.name: Columbia
columbia-missouri.manufacturing_summary: Wikipedia article identifies no significant manufacturing sector; economy historically dominated by education, healthcare, and insurance.
columbia-missouri.decision_rationale: No verifiable manufacturing employers or industrial activity. 301 to Missouri state page.

houston-texas.name: Houston
houston-texas.manufacturing_summary: Petrochemical hub since WWII when refineries and manufacturing plants were built along the ship channel. Major oil and gas equipment manufacturing center.

dallas-texas.name: Dallas
dallas-texas.manufacturing_summary: During WWII Dallas was a major military vehicle and aircraft manufacturing center; Ford produced 94,000+ jeeps and 6,000 military trucks; North American Aviation produced 18,000+ aircraft. Modern industrial base retains defense and aerospace presence.
dallas-texas.decision_rationale: Large metro with verifiable defense and aerospace heritage; Wikipedia article is light on current-manufacturer detail. Best paired with Fort Worth coverage for the DFW manufacturing story.

fort-worth-texas.name: Fort Worth
industrial_parks: Barnett Shale natural gas extraction area
fort-worth-texas.manufacturing_summary: Lockheed Martin Aeronautics has a major presence in Fort Worth (F-16/F-35 production heritage). Bell Textron manufactures rotorcraft. BNSF Railway is HQ'd here.

austin-texas.name: Austin
austin-texas.manufacturing_summary: Technology roots trace to Tracor (1962). IBM, Texas Instruments, and Motorola (now NXP) established semiconductor manufacturing 1967–1974. Tesla and Samsung operate major plants in the region.

san-antonio-texas.name: San Antonio
san-antonio-texas.manufacturing_summary: Toyota constructed a manufacturing plant on the South Side, anchoring an automotive manufacturing cluster. City has added a sizable manufacturing sector centered around automobiles.

el-paso-texas.name: El Paso
major_employers: University of Texas at El Paso
el-paso-texas.manufacturing_summary: Economy developed through copper smelting, oil refining, and garment manufacturing; cross-border ties with Ciudad Juárez. Long-haul state from Waterloo.
el-paso-texas.decision_rationale: Verifiable industrial base but the longest-haul city (1,288 miles). Best framed as ship-only service.
